newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Sidanko plans convertible bond, raises capital.
newsitem.headline: Sidanko plans convertible bond, raises capital.

text.p: Russian oil group Sidanko said on Monday it was raising its authorised capital to 26.17 billion roubles from 9.30 billion, and planned an issue of bonds convertible into ordinary shares.
The moves were agreed at an extraordinary shareholders meeting on December 28, OAO Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sidanko) said in a statement.
Sidanko said shareholders had agreed to issue 421.88 million new shares with a face value of 40 roubles each, raising authorised capital by 16.88 billion roubles.

It said 4.74 million of these shares, equivalent to 189.73 million roubles of the capital, would be transferred to the State Property Committee, Russia's privatisation ministry, to defend the state's interests in Sidanko.
Sidanko would also take steps to convert shares in its subsidiaries into a single Sidanko share, a process already adopted by some other Russian oil companies.
Sidanko is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years. Its main operating units are Chernogorneft, Kondpetroleum and Varyoganneftegaz.
It owns 38 percent of the capital, equivalent to 51 percent of the voting shares, of these and other subsidiaries.
Shares in Sidanko are not actively traded, but the three main subsidiaries are among the constituents of the Russian Trading System's 24-share index of Russia's most liquid stocks.
The government is currently accepting bids for 51 percent of Sidanko. The offer closes on January 9.

The tender has been overshadowed by a dispute about the ownership of oil company Purneftegaz. The Federal Property Fund, which is organising the tender, said Sidanko's assets include 38 percent, or 51 percent of the voting shares, of Purgneftegaz.
But state oil holding company Rosneft, which was previously allocated the Purneftegaz stake, has won a court order halting the transfer of Purneftegaz to Sidanko until the dispute is resolved.
In September ZAO Interros Oil, affiliated with the Interros financial-industrial group built around Uneximbank, won an investment tender for 34 percent of Sidanko.

MFK Bank, which is associated with Uneximbank, won the right last year to manage a 51 percent stake in Sidanko under the government's shares-for-loans programme, and this appears to be the stake now being tendered.
